reviewerDerivedProposition: Severe-range blood pressure confirmed on repeat after delivery, together with central nervous system features - headache, scotomata, hyperreflexia with clonus - and proteinuria, establishes postpartum preeclampsia with severe features. HELLP is excluded because the defining haemolysis, transaminase and platelet pattern is absent. Hypertension without severe features is excluded because severe-range pressures are paired with neurologic findings; a normotensive prenatal course and the absence of right upper quadrant pain are not what makes that distinction.
requiredFacts: Severe-range BP on repeat, CNS symptoms, hyperreflexia with clonus, 3+ proteinuria - stage1.

The laboratory panel that excludes HELLP - stage2 ONLY: platelets 195 x10^3/uL, AST 34 U/L, ALT 28 U/L, LDH 198 U/L, plus urine protein-to-creatinine ratio 0.42 and uric acid 6.8 mg/dL which the two HELLP distractors cite.
disclosureEvidence: The parent TITLE is 'Late postpartum preeclampsia with severe features presenting after discharge', and the Chinese title likewise reads '出院后出现的迟发性产后子痫前期伴重度特征'. The title states the keyed answer of the dx dropdown verbatim. A title is a global surface rendered at every boundary, so no anchor can hide it. MORE SERIOUSLY, the disclosure is not confined to the title. Sibling q1's STEM reads 'highlight the findings that form the urgent preeclampsia-with-severe-features cluster requiring immediate emergency evaluation', and sibling q2's rationale states that the presentation classifies 'as preeclampsia with severe features'. Under P23 a case study is one top-level question with one aggregate submit and true unfolding reveal is deferred, so every part is presented together and q1's stem is visible to a learner answering q3.
clinicalVerdict: All three keys are clinically correct and I verified each against the Stage 2 panel. Keyed dx_pre is right: repeat severe-range pressures after delivery with headache, scotomata, hyperreflexia and clonus plus proteinuria is postpartum preeclampsia with severe features, and the neurologic findings alone suffice for the severe classification. Keyed hellp_normal is right and is directly supported by the numbers: platelets 195 x10^3/uL are normal, AST 34 and ALT 28 U/L are essentially normal, and LDH 198 U/L is normal, so none of the three HELLP components is present. The two HELLP distractors are properly wrong - a urine protein-to-creatinine ratio of 0.42 speaks to preeclampsia rather than to HELLP, and an elevated uric acid of 6.8 mg/dL is an associated finding that forms no part of the HELLP definition, which is exactly the trap the testTakingStrategy warns against. Keyed sev_bp_cns is right, and the distractors are properly wrong since absence of right upper quadrant pain and a normotensive prenatal course do not bear on severity classification. THE DEFECT IS NOT CLINICAL BUT A DISCLOSURE OF THE DIAGNOSIS ACROSS SHARED AND SIBLING SURFACES.
contentDefects: PRIMARY: the bilingual parent title names the keyed diagnosis. Because the title is global it is visible at every boundary and cannot be repaired by anchoring.

PRIMARY AND MORE CONSEQUENTIAL: sibling q1's stem names 'the urgent preeclampsia-with-severe-features cluster'. Since all parts of a case render together under P23, neutralising the title alone would leave the dx dropdown disclosed by a sibling stem. Codex's proposed repair is therefore necessary but NOT SUFFICIENT.
CONTRIBUTING: four further siblings (q2, q4, q5, q6) name preeclampsia in their stems, options or rationales, so the diagnosis pervades the parent.
bilingualVerdict: PARALLEL - stem, clozeStem, all nine dropdown options, all three keys, rationale, three byChoice entries, strategy and glossary are semantically equivalent EN/ZH. The title discloses the diagnosis equally in both languages, so any title repair must be bilingual.
sourcesChecked: No external fetch was load-bearing. The HELLP exclusion was verified arithmetically against the Stage 2 panel in the frozen packet - normal platelets, normal transaminases, normal LDH - rather than against an external criterion set, so the finding rests on the authored source. The severe-features classification by severe-range BP plus CNS findings is standard obstetric criteria and was not contested.
siblingImpact: HIGH - THE HIGHEST IN THIS TRANCHE. The title is a global surface visible to all six parts. I checked every sibling directly: q1, q2, q4, q5 and q6 all name preeclampsia in their own text, and q1 does so in its STEM, which is pre-submit visible. All five are non-residual and already accepted, so any repair that reaches them is a change to accepted content and needs its own review. This is why I record the title fix as insufficient: the sibling surface, not the title, is the binding constraint.
repairConstraints: Neutralise the bilingual parent title to a presenting-symptom title that does not name the diagnosis, for example a postpartum readmission for severe headache and elevated blood pressure. Apply in EN and ZH.

THEN address the sibling disclosure, which the title change does not fix. Either neutralise sibling q1's stem so it does not name the diagnostic cluster, which is a change to accepted content requiring its own independent review, OR re-scope q3 so it no longer asks the learner to name the diagnosis and instead assesses only the differential-exclusion reasoning in the hellp_evidence and severity_evidence dropdowns. The second route is confined to the residual row and is my recommendation.
Preserve all actual clinical data; no laboratory value, vital sign or finding may change.
Preserve all three dropdown keys if the dx dropdown is retained; each is independently verified correct.
Survey and record the impact on all five siblings before any shared-surface edit is applied.
Anchor to stage2 after repair. Baseline is not available because the HELLP exclusion rests entirely on the Stage 2 panel.
criticalNote: This row is the clearest instance in the review of a defect that anchoring cannot touch. The leak is through a global title and a sibling stem, both of which render regardless of this part's boundary, so the boundary question and the disclosure question are independent here.
agreementReasoning: I noticed the diagnostic title while reading the parent and reached stage2 as the boundary independently; Codex identifies the same title defect, proposes the same boundary, and correctly instructs that the sibling impact of the shared-title change be surveyed. I performed that survey and it returned a result that changes the repair: the diagnosis is named not only in the title but in five sibling parts, including q1's pre-submit stem, and because P23 renders all parts of a case together the title fix alone leaves q3 disclosed. I therefore record Codex's proposed repair as necessary but insufficient and supply the additional constraint, with a recommended route that keeps the fix inside the residual row rather than editing accepted sibling content. I also verified all three dropdown keys against the Stage 2 panel rather than accepting them.
